{
  "candidate_rtl": "module mul_subexpression(
    input [7:0] multiplicand,
    input [7:0] multiplier,
    output [15:0] product
);

wire [15:0] pp0;
wire [15:0] pp1;
wire [15:0] pp2;
wire [15:0] pp3;
wire [15:0] pp4;
wire [15:0] pp5;
wire [15:0] pp6;
wire [15:0] pp7;

assign pp0 = {8'b0, multiplicand}        & {16{multiplier[0]}};
assign pp1 = {7'b0, multiplicand, 1'b0}  & {16{multiplier[1]}};
assign pp2 = {6'b0, multiplicand, 2'b0}  & {16{multiplier[2]}};
assign pp3 = {5'b0, multiplicand, 3'b0}  & {16{multiplier[3]}};
assign pp4 = {4'b0, multiplicand, 4'b0}  & {16{multiplier[4]}};
assign pp5 = {3'b0, multiplicand, 5'b0}  & {16{multiplier[5]}};
assign pp6 = {2'b0, multiplicand, 6'b0}  & {16{multiplier[6]}};
assign pp7 = {1'b0, multiplicand, 7'b0}  & {16{multiplier[7]}};

wire [15:0] sum01;
wire [15:0] sum23;
wire [15:0] sum45;
wire [15:0] sum67;
wire [15:0] sum0123;
wire [15:0] sum4567;

assign sum01 = pp0 + pp1;
assign sum23 = pp2 + pp3;
assign sum45 = pp4 + pp5;
assign sum67 = pp6 + pp7;
assign sum0123 = sum01 + sum23;
assign sum4567 = sum45 + sum67;
assign product = sum0123 + sum4567;

endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The original implementation forms a seven-stage serial accumulation chain, so the critical path traverses nearly all intermediate 16-bit additions.",
  "rewrite": "The eight shifted partial products are preserved exactly, but their additions are organized as a balanced binary tree with three adder levels instead of a seven-adder serial chain.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Reduced maximum data arrival is expected because the longest arithmetic path contains three balanced additions rather than seven sequential additions. Input and output combinational behavior remains unchanged.",

  "functional_boundaries": "All inputs are treated as arbitrary unsigned 8-bit binary values. Each partial product is explicitly zero-extended and shifted within 16 bits; all additions and the product output are 16 bits, matching the original truncation behavior. No assumptions are made about input values."
